# Changelog

All notable changes to `@idosgames/core` are documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project follows [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

> While the version stays in the **`0.x`** range the public API is still stabilizing:
> breaking changes may land in a **minor** bump. Once the surface is stable we cut
> `1.0.0`, and from then on breaking changes require a **major** bump.
>
> Anything marked `@experimental` in the code is exempt from these guarantees until it
> is promoted. See [RELEASING.md](../../RELEASING.md) for the full process.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.21.2] - 2026-10-05

The model follows the backend rename (rolled out 05.10.2026). Patch, not minor: the server no longer
sends the old field, so the old name was already always empty — nothing that worked stops working.

### Changed

- `BlockchainDefinitions.IframeAllowedHosts` → **`IframeConnectHosts`**. It now widens only the
  game's network requests (`connect-src`) while it is embedded on idosgames.com. Framing another
  website there is never allowed (`frame-src` is platform hosts only, owner's decision): a game build
  must be the game itself, not a wrapper around an external site.

## [0.21.1] - 2026-10-05

Crypto withdrawal fees and IOUs (rollout 05.10.2026). Additive: new optional fields only.

### Added

- `CryptoCurrencyDefinition`: `DeveloperWithdrawalFeePercent`, `CommunityMarketingWithdrawalFeePercent`,
  `WithdrawalBurnPercent` — fees are taken on the player's withdrawal only; `UnbackedRewardCurrencyID` — the
  `{ID}_IOU` virtual currency a crypto reward is paid in when the players' reward pool cannot cover it
  (repaid with real crypto later; crypto spent in the game spends the IOU first).
- `CurrencyDefinitions`: `CryptoRewardsFromDeveloperShare`, `CryptoIouForScriptsAndAI`,
  `CryptoAutoRepayIouOnWithdrawal` toggles.

## [0.21.0] - 2026-10-03

The central cache, and behaviour fixes found by playing every system of the playground on the
local stand. A game with every system used to send ~25 requests right after login; now the login is
ONE `GetClientState` that brings the state (unchanged containers are not even re-sent), the config
(by version) and the server views the game reads.

### Added

- **`client.cache` — the central cache** (`DataCache`). Every read decides there between the local
  copy and the server:
  - **title config** — `configSection(key)`: served while the config version is unchanged; sections
    outside the client projection (`TimedBoost`, `Marketplace`, `Match`, `AI`) that a system fetched
    are kept under that same version (`SectionCache`, storage key `idos:sec:{titleID}`);
  - **player state** — `ensureState(containers, { maxAgeMs?, force? })`: a container is fresh while
    its `Rev` is confirmed by the server in this session (login, a slice read, or a mutation reply
    `+1`); the stale containers of every caller in one tick go out as ONE versioned
    `User/GetUserState`. `defineStateRule(container, { needsServer, refresh })` declares a container
    the server must compute on read — built in: `Quest` (a cycle ended), `Tutorial` (lazy transitions,
    once a session), `Reward` (comeback presence on read), `Character` (a hero given by default),
    `Collection` (the active collection may have changed);
  - **server views** — `defineView({ key, ttlMs?, expiresAt?, dependsOn?, invalidateOn? })` +
    `read(view, fetch, opts)`: one request for every concurrent reader, lifetime from the data, the
    TTL, the `Rev` of the containers it depends on and SDK events; `peek`, `put`, `invalidate`,
    `clear`, `describe`. Built in: storefront, active deals, active events, active season, leaderboard
    progress, mailbox / chat / inbox unread, marketplace my-state, coop user state.
- **Server views ride on the login.** `UserRequest.Views` / `ClientState.Views` (engine
  `ClientStateViews`): the login answer carries the views asked for — `[{ Name: "*" }]` all of them,
  or exactly the listed ones; a view with variants and no parameter comes for every variant (each
  season chain, all enabled leaderboards). Each is the same `Data` as its own endpoint, validated
  with the same schema and applied by the same service code; a failing view does not fail the login.
  Which views to ask for is the client option `loginViews`: `"auto"` (default — the views the game
  read in the last 3 sessions, remembered under `idos:views:{titleID}`), `"all"`, `"none"` or a list.
  `CachedView.login` + `DataCache.bindLoginView` declare a view as one the login can bring.
- A view invalidated while its request is in flight (most often by its OWN reply: a read that writes
  the player document reports the new version) keeps the answer for a short settle window instead of
  dropping it; a value `put` later wins. Views also drop on the SDK events of the actions behind them
  (`invalidateOn`), not only on the `Rev` of their containers. Mailbox replies put fresh counters.
- `ReadOptions` (`forceRefresh`, `maxAgeMs`) on those reads; `tutorial.getUserTutorialState` is a
  cached view too (dropped when the `Tutorial` `Rev` moves).

### Changed

- **Definitions are served from the title config cache.** Every `getDefinitions` whose data is a
  section of the title config (season, leaderboard, collection, coop event, quest, character,
  tutorial, timed event, store, chat, mailbox, timed boost, match, AI, lootbox, craft, premium,
  reward, referral) answers from the cache without a request; `{ forceRefresh: true }` goes to the
  server. `TitleConfig.getSection` returns a section wherever it came from (fetched or with the
  config).
- The server views listed above are cached by their policy instead of hitting the server on every
  call; pass `{ forceRefresh: true }` to bypass.
- `applyUserStateContainers` emits `user:inventoryUpdated` when the slice carried the inventory.
- `user.getUserState` (the versioned slice) replaces only the containers whose version moved: an
  unchanged one keeps its live copy instead of the stored snapshot.
- The transport announces `user:stateVersions` BEFORE the quest/tutorial side channels, so a
  listener that re-reads on `tutorial:systemProgress` already sees the dependent views dropped.

### Fixed

- **Parallel calls with different arguments are no longer dropped.** The transport's throttle / dedup
  key was the route alone, so the active season of two chains, the active coop event per chain, two
  boards read at once — every call after the first came back "Duplicate request skipped". The default key
  is now the route plus the request without its per-call `RelatedEntityID` (`requestKey`); the same request
  twice is still deduplicated.
- **No burst over the engine's per-player limit.** The engine blocks a player for 10 s after more than 20
  requests in one second, and a game with many systems sends about that many right after login. The
  transport now paces request starts (`maxRequestsPerSecond`, default 15); a 429 is retried on a schedule
  that outlasts the block (1.5 s / 4 s / 6 s); a 409 "Operation in progress" (the engine's per-player lock)
  is retried like a transient — the handler did not run.
- **Friends counters follow friend actions.** `send/accept/decline/removeFriend` apply the server's
  `Counters` (and the local patches move `IncomingCount` / `FriendsCount` / `OutgoingCount`): the friends
  badge used to keep showing a request already answered.
- **An unlocked character is level 1 in the cache** (as on the server) — it used to read as still locked
  until the next full state read.
- **`RealtimeSession` emits `left`** when this side leaves the room (`leave()`, page close), so whoever holds
  the session (a game that took the room) knows it is over. A `SendSignal` to a member who has just left is
  no longer reported as `error:global`.

## [0.20.0] - 2026-10-02

Models and services checked against the engine's real C# handlers (types, requests, endpoints) and
against a deployed DEV title (`packages/harness`, `npm run e2e:module`).

### Changed (breaking types)

- **`purchase.getDefinitions()`** now returns `PurchaseDefinitionsResponse` (`{ Purchase, Availability }`).
  The engine wraps `GetDefinitions` / `GetUserState` with the platform availability; the old code parsed
  the bare shape and silently got empty data. `getUserState()` still returns the unwrapped state.
- **Marketplace `MyLeadingBids` → `MyBids`** (the engine's name); `getMyState(bidsFilter?)` and
  `getHistory(token, size, historyFilter?)` gained the filters the engine accepts.

### Added

- **`client.debugCall(module, action, body?)`** — a raw `Client/{module}/{action}` call as the signed-in
  player: no response schema, no auto-retry, its own throttle key. For tooling, not games: the AI Coder's
  `CallGameApi` reaches it through `@idosgames/app-shell`'s agent bridge (published only inside the live
  preview iframe).
- **Config `null`s are read the way the engine reads them.** The engine tolerates `null` list elements and
  `null` dictionary values in a title config ("no entry"); one such `null` used to make the whole module
  response unreadable (Lootbox, Reward, TimedEvent, Currency, Match). When a response fails validation as
  received, the transport drops `null`s from lists and dictionaries and validates once more
  (`transport/dropNulls.ts`); a response that validated before is read exactly as before.
- **`ClientState.User.TimedBoost`** (engine) is applied like every other container — active boosts survive a
  game restart without a `timedBoost.getActive()` call. `ClientState.User.Character` is always present
  (empty for a new player).

### Fixed

- **`ScheduleMode`** knew 3 of the engine's 6 modes: an `AlwaysOn` event was read as `Cyclic` and its
  `Type` could not be passed to `timedEvent.grantTokens` / `claimMilestone`.
- **Tutorial**: closing a step that pays (a step `Effects.Grant` or the flow's `AutoClaim` reward) left the
  cached balance stale — the response carries only the flow view. The inventory is now re-read once.
- **Blockchain**: deposit / withdrawal / confirm apply the server's `StateDelta` only, so a replayed request
  cannot credit or debit the cache twice; crypto balances are always strings.
- **TimedEvent**: a milestone claim marks only the instance it was claimed in (`TokenEntityID`).
- **Leaderboard**: `claimMilestone(id, milestoneId, cycleKey?)` for past-cycle grace claims; a past-cycle claim
  no longer marks the current cycle.
- **Social**: sending a request to someone who already asked you accepts it instead of adding an outgoing one.
- **Character**: equipped-item `Level` is mirrored after `item.upgradeLevel`.
- **AI**: `Reward` (re-reads the inventory once), `OutputJson`, `Variables`, `Context`.
- Reward, TimedBoost, GameLoop, DataCollections, Quest, CoopEvent, CommunityMarketing, Premium models brought
  in line with the engine (missing / renamed fields; fields the engine strips for clients are not modelled).

### Deprecated

- `premium.purchaseRealMoney` — the engine does not route `Premium/PurchaseRealMoney`.

## [0.19.0] - 2026-09-27

Realtime multiplayer: a ready-made WebRTC transport on top of the engine's Multiplayer signaling,
plus the room actions it needs (host handover, kick/ban). First user: VoxelCraft co-op.

### Added

- **`@idosgames/core/realtime`** — new subpath, `RealtimeSession.create()` / `.join()`:
  - two DataChannels per link: `rel` (ordered, reliable, fragmented up to 16 KB frames) and `fast`
    (unordered, no retransmits);
  - `Host` (star) and `Mesh` topologies, glare-free offers;
  - signaling through a single-flight, per-peer batched outbox; descriptions carry their ICE
    candidates, so about one `SendSignal` per side per connection;
  - adaptive polling: 1 s only while setting up, then 2.5 s for the host and 20 s for others;
  - keepalive and RTT (`linkStats`), reconnect with back-off, standby links (`setExtraPeers`);
  - host handover: `setSuccessor()` + `leave()`, a `keepalive` leave on `pagehide`, and
    `claimHost()` when the host tab dies;
  - `kick()` / `unban()`: the kicked player is told over its link and polls at once — the server
    alone confirms the removal;
  - TURN servers taken as is from the room snapshot.
- `client.multiplayer.claimHost()`, `kickMember(roomID, target, ban?)`, `unbanMember()`;
  `leaveRoom(roomID, { successorUserID?, keepalive? })`.
- Models: `KickMemberResponse`, `UnbanMemberResponse`, `RoomSnapshotResponse.BannedUserIDs` (host
  and owner only); request fields `SuccessorUserID`, `Ban`; actions `ClaimHost`, `KickMember`,
  `UnbanMember`.
- Events: `multiplayer:hostClaimed`, `multiplayer:memberKicked`, `multiplayer:memberUnbanned`.
- Transport: `PostOptions.keepalive` (a request that outlives the page).

### Changed

- `sendSignal` is throttled per target (`Multiplayer:SendSignal:{target}`) instead of one shared
  key: signals to different peers no longer drop each other.
- Build: `flatten-dts` now flattens every emitted `.d.ts` / `.d.cts`, including shared chunks. The
  shared `ClientContext-*` chunk had grown to 3.4 MB of zod types.

## [0.18.0] - 2026-09-23

### Added

- **Title login mode and play access by token balance** (`cfg.Blockchain.PlayAccess`):
  `PlatformLoginResponse.PlayAccess`, `client.auth.playAccess` + `playAccess:changed`,
  `playAccess:required` (a gameplay call refused with HTTP 403 `PLAY_ACCESS_REQUIRED` — not raised as
  `error:global`), `client.auth.getAuthOptions()` (the mode before login),
  `client.auth.linkWallet()`, `client.blockchain.getPlayAccess()` / `confirmPlayAccess()`,
  `WalletGateBalanceSource.InGame`.
- **Session refresh by refresh token** (`Authentication/RefreshSession`). Logins now return
  `RefreshToken`; the client keeps it (storage only when remembering), rotates it on every refresh,
  and uses it FIRST on a 401 and on `autoLogin()`. Replaying the login method is the fallback. Any
  remembered session comes back, wallet and Google included. The token is forgotten only on refusals
  that mean it is dead (invalid/expired/revoked/reused/missing, banned) — a transient refusal keeps it.

### Removed

- `BlockchainWalletLoginPolicy.TokenGates` — token requirements live in `PlayAccess` only.

## [0.17.0] - 2026-09-23

A game on the SDK can now hand idosgames.com a frame of itself for the site's **Shot** button
("take a shot and share"). The request comes from the parent page, so the same release gives every
game↔site bridge ONE list of platform origins instead of a copy per bridge.

### Added

- **`PLATFORM_ORIGINS`** and **`isPlatformParentOrigin(origin)`** — the origins of the platform's
  own pages, checked by every bridge a game exposes to its parent (push, wallet, the new screenshot
  responder in `@idosgames/app-shell`). The push bridge and the wallet's frame guard used to carry
  their own copies; they now read this one, with unchanged behaviour.
  `isPlatformParentOrigin` also accepts a `localhost` parent, but **only while the game itself is
  served from localhost** — a shipped build on `{id}.idos.games` answers nothing except the real
  site, so a page on the player's own machine cannot ask it for anything. The wallet keeps checking
  `PLATFORM_ORIGINS` directly and does not gain the local allowance.

### Removed

- **`PlatformBridgeDefinitions.AllowShowTitlesPlayed` / `AllowShowWorkshopWorks`** (config section
  `PlatformBridge`) — the publisher no longer decides what a player may show about themselves on
  idosgames.com. The "Uses" and "Workshop" tabs of a public profile are shown by default; the player
  alone can hide them, in their profile settings on the site. Nothing to do in a game client: these
  fields were never read there, and the server ignores them if an old config still carries them.

## [0.16.0] - 2026-09-20

The social layer became one subsystem shared by the platform and every title, so the Workshop no
longer carries its own copy of likes, follows and reports. Timeline was replaced by an inbox.

⚠ **Breaking.** A game that calls the removed Workshop methods stops compiling; the replacements
take an entity type, so the same action now works on any object, not just a publication.

### Removed

- **`client.workshop.like` / `unlike` / `favorite` / `follow` / `unfollow` / `report`** — moved to
  `client.social`, which addresses an object by type:
  `client.social.like("WorkshopItem", contentID)`, `client.social.follow("User", creatorUserID)`,
  `client.social.report("WorkshopItem", contentID, "Broken")`.
- Types that belonged to those methods: `WorkshopReactionKind`, `WorkshopReportReason`,
  `WorkshopReactionResponse`, `WorkshopFollowResponse`, `WorkshopReportResponse`. The social
  equivalents are `SocialReactionKind`, `SocialReportReason`, `SocialReactionView`,
  `SocialActorPage`, `SocialReportResponse`.
- **`TimelineEventType`, `TimelineResponse`, `SocialTimelineEvent`** and the cached
  `UserData.Social.Timeline` — the timeline is now an inbox (below). The event
  `social:timelineLoaded` became `social:inboxLoaded`; `workshop:reacted` is gone.

### Added

- **Inbox instead of a timeline**: `client.social.getInbox()`, `getInboxUnread()`,
  `markInboxSeen()`. Unread is counted from a "seen up to" mark held by the server, not from a
  counter other people increment in your document. New events: `social:inboxLoaded`,
  `social:inboxBadge`.
- **Reactions, comments and reports on any object** (`SocialEntityType`: `User`, `Channel`, `Title`,
  `WorkshopItem`, `Post`, `Comment`): `like` / `unlike` / `favorite` / `unfavorite`,
  `addComment` / `editComment` / `deleteComment` / `getComments`, `report`, plus `getMyReactions`
  and `getEntityStates` for showing what the player already did. Events `social:entityStateChanged`,
  `social:commentAdded`, `social:commentEdited`, `social:commentDeleted`, `social:reported`.
- **Follows and blocks on the same addressing**: `follow` / `unfollow` / `block` / `unblock`,
  `getFollowers` / `getFollowing` / `getBlocked` with a `SocialCursor`.
- **Platform bridge**: `PlatformBridgeDefinitions` in the title configuration —
  `PlatformProfileMode`, `PlatformFriendsMode`, `FriendSource`, and `FRIENDS_FROM_PLATFORM` (the
  refusal a title returns when friends come from the platform account). `client.social
.friendRequestsAllowed()` tells the UI whether in-game friend requests exist at all.
- **`SocialDefinitions`** in the title configuration: comment rules for the UI (on/off, which
  objects, text length, links). Counters, follows and reports work without it.

## [0.15.0] - 2026-09-16

### Added

- **`client.purchase.buyWithTelegramStars(productID, { open? })`**: buys a product priced in
  Telegram Stars — asks the server for an invoice link and opens it via
  `Telegram.WebApp.openInvoice` (or returns the link for the host to open itself with
  `open: false`). Nothing is granted locally: Telegram reports the payment to the title bot's
  webhook and the server grants from there, same as store receipts.
- `IapStore` gained a `"TelegramStars"` member, and `IapProductDefinition` gained an optional
  `TelegramStarsPrice` — unset means the product isn't sold for Stars.

## [0.14.2] - 2026-09-16

Found by the first live run of the Workshop against a deployed backend.

### Changed

- **`client.workshop`**: a failed upload/download of workshop files (`publish`, `downloadFiles`)
  now says that a storage bucket without a CORS rule for the page's origin is the usual cause if the
  network is fine. A browser reports that rejection as a bare network error, which read like a dropped
  connection.

## [0.14.1] - 2026-09-16

Custom analytics events, A/B variants on the client, and data collections. A patch on purpose:
everything is additive, and a minor on `0.x` would force a range + version bump of wallet,
module-sdk, react and app-shell.

### Added

- **`client.analytics`** (`AnalyticsService`) — Firebase-style custom events: `logEvent(name,
params, value)`, `logScreenView`, `flush`, player consent via `setEnabled`. Batched (25 events /
  30 s / tab hidden) and stored in `platform.storage`, retried with the same `BatchID` (the server
  dedupes). Automatic events (`idos_first_open`, `idos_session_start`, `idos_app_update`,
  `idos_os_update`) are sent only once the title config has `Analytics.Enabled === true`. The queue
  belongs to the player: a different player signing in drops the previous player's tail. Exports
  `AnalyticsEventNaming`, `AutomaticEvent`, `AnalyticsLimits`, `AnalyticsDropReason`,
  `AnalyticsAction`, `EVENT_NAME_PATTERN`, `describeUserAgent`; events `analytics:flushed`,
  `analytics:eventsDropped`. `TitlePublicConfigurationModel.Analytics` (optional). Skill
  `analytics-events`.
- **`client.experiments`** (`ExperimentsService`) — the A/B variants in effect for this player:
  `load()` once per session (`GetExperiments`), then `getVariant`, `getStatus`, `getParams`,
  `getParam(id, key, default)` (typed by the default), `isInVariant`. Before the answer, getters
  return this player's values from the previous session or the default. Events
  `experiments:loaded`, `experiments:changed`. `ExperimentDefinition` gains optional `Goals`,
  `ActivationEvent`, `RolloutVariantID`; new `ExperimentGoalKind`, `PlayerExperimentStatus`,
  `ExperimentAction`. Skill `experiments-system`.
- **`client.dataCollections`** (`DataCollectionsService`) — the title's own data structures
  (guilds, auctions, orders, catalogs, articles…) with declared fields, sort keys and access rules:
  `getDefinitions`, `get`, `getMany`, `query`, `queryAll`, `count`, `create`, `update`, `set`,
  `increment`, `delete`, `batch`, `getCounter`, `getMyRoles`, files (`beginFileUpload`,
  `uploadFile`), and login-free reads of public collections (`getPublicViews`, `readPublicView`,
  `getPublic`, `searchPublic`). `where(field, op, value)` builds a filter. Not to be confused with
  `client.collection` (collectible card sets). Skill `data-collections`.

## [0.14.0] - 2026-09-14

Workshop — a catalog of player and publisher content handed out as licenses.

### Added

- **`client.workshop`** (`WorkshopService`) — browse the catalog (`browse`, `getContent`,
  `getCollection`, `getCreatorProfile`), publish in one call (`publish`: declare → upload by signed
  URLs → verify; `contentID` uploads a new revision; a `client.ai` asset can be published by URL),
  `updateContent`, `unpublish`, `getMyContent`, get access (`acquire(contentID, option)` — sends the
  option's price as `ExpectedPrice`, so a changed price is refused instead of charged), download
  (`getDownload`, `downloadFiles`), `getMyLicenses`, likes, favorites, following authors, `report`.
  Access options are ANY-of: `Free`, `Price`, `Holding` (`WhileHeld` — checked on every download, no
  license; `UnlockOnce`). Definitions come from `getDefinitions()` only — the section is not part of
  the public title config. Events `workshop:definitionsLoaded`, `workshop:published`,
  `workshop:updated`, `workshop:acquired`, `workshop:reacted`. Skill `workshop-system`.

## [0.13.0] - 2026-09-13

InApp AI generation.

### Added

- **`client.ai`** (`AIService`) — text (with optional chat history and input images), image
  generation and editing, video, speech (TTS), music, and 3D-model generation by `FeatureKey`.
  Which features/models/prices are available is configured by the publisher and read from
  `getDefinitions()` — the client never chooses a model. Video, 3D, and `Async` text return a
  `running` job: poll `getVideo` / `getThreeD` / `getText` yourself while the player is waiting
  (`isAIGenerationTerminal(status)` to know when to stop — every poll is billed against the
  publisher's API quota). Exports `AIAction`, `AIModality`, `AIGenerationStatus`, `AIErrorCode`,
  `isAIGenerationTerminal`, `parseAIErrorCode`; events `ai:definitionsLoaded`,
  `ai:generationUpdated`, `ai:generationCompleted`, `ai:generationFailed`. Skill
  `ai-generation-system`.

## [0.12.0] - 2026-09-12

Character skins, level-aware crafting, and an exact inventory cache: every response that carries an
instance delta is now applied in one step, so an unstackable grant no longer shows up twice.
Breaking — see below.

### Breaking

- **Item `CustomData` is a string map, not a string.** `ItemDefinition.CustomData` and the
  unstackable instance's `CustomData` are now `Record<string, string>` — the shape the engine
  actually sends. Read the keys directly instead of parsing a string.

### Added

- **Character skins** — `client.character.unlockSkin(characterID, skinID, { selectedOptionID,
payment, autoEquip })`, `equipSkin`, `unequipSkin`, `getCharacterSkins`; exports `SKIN_SLOT`,
  `isReservedSlot`, `SKIN_ALREADY_OWNED`; events `character:skinUnlocked` / `skinEquipped` /
  `skinUnequipped`. A skin is an item equipped in `Equipment[SKIN_SLOT]` — hide `@` keys from slot
  UIs with `isReservedSlot`, but keep them in Power. Draw the "Buy" button from
  `getCharacterSkins().Purchasable`, not from config. `SKIN_ALREADY_OWNED` is a normal outcome,
  not an error. Skill `character-system` (section "Skins").
- **Craft output level** — `CraftDefinition.OutputLevelMode` / `InputSelection` /
  `OutputLevelOverflow` (string enums exported as `CraftOutputLevelMode`,
  `CraftInputSelectionMode`, `CraftOutputLevelOverflow`), `CraftSingleResult.OutputLevel` /
  `BurnedInstances`, and `craft(…, inputInstanceIDs?)` for `ClientSelected` recipes. ⚠
  `inputItemIDs` are catalog `ItemID`s, never instances. An unknown setting value from a newer
  engine falls back to its default instead of failing the whole definitions parse.
- **`Inventory` instance delta** on every response that carries one (and on `zBatchResponse`),
  applied through `UserData.applyResourcesWithDelta`.

### Fixed

- An unstackable grant (lootbox, skin purchase, …) no longer appears twice in the cache, and a
  spend no longer drops an extra copy: the delta now reconciles the cache's guesses instead of
  being applied on top of them.
- `purchase.validatePurchasesBatch` now applies every granted receipt to the cache — it applied
  nothing before.

## [0.11.0] - 2026-09-10

Player chat, the creator reward programme, and push notifications all land at once, alongside a
from-scratch Store rewrite and the removal of DealOffer's pre-`Purchase`-module legacy. Breaking —
see below.

### Breaking

- **DealOffer sheds its pricing/ads legacy and moves to blocks.** `DealOfferGraphMode`/
  `DealOfferDefinition.GraphMode` are gone — the graph's shape is now derived from
  `RootNodeIDs`/`NextNodeIDs`/`ChoiceGroupID`, never declared, so it cannot disagree with how the
  offer actually plays. `DealPurchaseActionDefinition`/`DealNodeActionDefinition.Purchase` are
  gone — a node's price is `DealNodeDefinition.PriceOptions` like everywhere else on the platform,
  and a node with a price and no options no longer silently charges nothing. Rewarded-video
  `AdPlacementID`/`RequireServerVerification` are gone — a video watch is now an ordinary
  `RewardedVideoCredit` price, verified structurally by `Advertising`, not by a flag nobody read.
  `DealOfferDefinition`'s flat fields (`Name`, `Description`, `Milestones` as a dict,
  `MilestoneClaimMode`, `MilestoneToken`, `AssetPaths`, `Metadata`) are replaced by
  `Identity`/`Availability`/`Behaviour`/`Graph`/`Milestones`/`Pricing`/`Reward` blocks plus
  `PresetBindings` — same shape as `Character`/`Store`. Read node/offer pricing and milestone
  settings from the blocks; the server resolves "not set" (inherit the preset) vs. "set" (final,
  including empty) — there is no client-side default to fall back on.
- **`CurrencyConversion.FeePercent` is now `Fee`, and it is a FRACTION** — `0.05` means 5%, not
  `5`. Same platform-wide `Percent` → `Rate`-family rename as `SpendRewardDefinition.Rate` in
  0.10.0; render a percentage if you like, but keep the wire value a fraction.
- **`CryptoNetworkBinding.MinDeposit` and `.WithdrawFee` are gone.** Dropped on the server; nothing
  here read them, so there is no replacement to reach for.

### Added

- **`client.chat`** (`ChatService`) — title channels and 1-on-1 conversations: `getChatDefinitions`,
  `getChannels`, `poll`, `getHistory`, `sendMessage`, `sendDirect`, `openDirectChannel`,
  `getConversations`, `markRead`, `joinChannel`, `leaveChannel`, `reportMessage`, `ignoreUser`,
  `unignoreUser`, plus `chat:*` events. ⚠ One `poll()` covers ALL rooms and never marks anything
  read — looping per channel or per tick multiplies the publisher's API bill for nothing. Port of
  the engine's `Chat` module. Skill `chat-system`.
- **`client.communityMarketing`** (`CommunityMarketingService`) — the game's half of the creator
  reward programme: `getState`, `getEarnings`, `claim`, `withdrawCryptoReward`,
  `checkJoinEligibility` (only meaningful for `Automatic` participation mode), plus
  `communityMarketing:*` events. ⚠⚠ `Granted` is the promise, `Earned`/`Mature` are estimates that
  can fall as a platform scrubs fake engagement — `Claimable` is derived from `Granted`, never
  `Mature`. A crypto reward never touches the in-game balance (`withdrawCryptoReward`, not
  `claim`) and debits the programme pool the moment the voucher is issued, before anything reaches
  the chain — an interrupted withdrawal is finished by `TitleTransactionID`, never retried as a
  fresh request. Port of the engine's `CommunityMarketing` module. Skill
  `community-marketing-system`.
- **`client.push`** (`PushService`) — `getConfig`, `getState`, `subscribe`, `unsubscribe`,
  `unsubscribeByHash`, `getSubscriptions`, plus the `push:configLoaded` / `push:subscribed` /
  `push:unsubscribed` events. Port of the engine's `Push` module.
- **`templates/host-starter/public/sw.js`** — a service worker the game OWNS, shipped in the seed.
  ⚠ It has no `fetch` handler and must never get one: a cached `index.html` points at
  content-hashed chunks the next deploy deletes, and the player gets a white screen from inside
  their own browser, where neither a CDN purge nor Ctrl+F5 reaches.
- Skill `push-notifications`.
- **`client.store.getStorefront()`** (`StoreService`) — the shop as this player sees it right now:
  resolved rotation, per-slot refresh timers, first-purchase/sold-out badges and remaining limits.
  ⚠ Draw this, not `getDefinitions()` — rotation is recomputed by the server on every read and
  nothing here can be derived on the client. Also `cachedStorefront`, `nextRefreshAtUtc()`, and a
  new `store:storefrontLoaded` event. `StoreService.purchase()` gains an optional `slot` (
  `storeID`/`sectionID`/`slotID`) so a pooled product's per-window cap applies unambiguously; the
  server re-checks the roll either way and answers a stale card with `OFFER_NOT_IN_ROTATION` —
  reload the shop on that code, do not show it as an error. Full model surface for the new
  `Stores -> Layout.Sections -> Slots` tree and the `StoreOffers` catalog (`StoreDefinition`,
  `StoreSlotDefinition`, `StorefrontView` and friends) is now exported from the package root.
  Rewritten skill `store-system`.

### Changed

- **`PlaytimeTracker`'s idle threshold is now 30 minutes, not 5** — matches the server's session
  boundary (`Usage.SessionIdleTimeoutMinutes`, the same rule Firebase/GA4 use) and the Unity SDK.
  The server decides session COUNT from the gap in the player's own activity and ignores the
  client's flag either way; the constant still matters for `SessionDurationSeconds`, so web and
  mobile numbers stay comparable.

### Notes

- ⚠⚠ **`subscribe()` must run from a real tap.** Browsers reject the permission prompt outside a
  user gesture, and Chrome permanently blocks an origin after a few dismissals — an automatic
  prompt does not merely fail, it removes the player's ability to ever say yes.
- ⚠⚠ **Inside the portal iframe the browser blocks the prompt outright**, so `subscribe()` asks
  the website to subscribe on its own top-level document; the engine still does the sending.
  `PushSubscribeResult.Where` says which path ran.
- The VAPID public key arrives from the server, never baked into the build; `EndpointHash` comes
  from the server and is never computed on the client.
- ⚠ **Chat's cloned/group channel type is scaffolded but has no provider yet** — the engine has no
  concept of clans, so a `Group` channel is hidden rather than shown empty until one exists.

## [0.10.0] - 2026-08-31

Where a player came from is now captured and delivered automatically, and playtime finally reaches
the publisher's analytics. Referral codes become short human codes with a server-built invite link.
Breaking — see below.

### Breaking

- **`SpendRewardDefinition.Percent` is now `Rate`, and it is a FRACTION.** `0.05` means 5%, not
  `5`. The old field never reached the server: it was dropped at deserialisation, so every kickback
  rule written through it silently paid nobody. Render a percentage if you like, but keep the wire
  value a fraction.
- **`UserData.patchReferralSubscription` takes the referrer's ID, not the code.** While a code and
  a `UserID` were the same string, echoing the code back happened to be right; with a short code it
  writes a code into an ID field. The activation response now carries `ReferrerUserID` separately
  from `ReferralCode`.
- **A referral code is no longer a `UserID`.** `activateReferralCode` accepts only the short code
  (or the invite link containing it); an internal identifier is rejected before any lookup. Nothing
  had shipped on the old form, so there is no migration path and none is needed.

### Added

- **`AcquisitionCapture`** — reads the launch URL and Telegram launch parameters when the client is
  created (`utm_*`, `gclid`/`fbclid`/`ttclid`/`msclkid`/`yclid`, `?ref=`, `idos_click`,
  `document.referrer`), keeps them across the login screen with a 30-day TTL, and attaches them to
  whichever sign-in the player uses. Nothing to wire; nothing to call.
- **`PlaytimeTracker`** — counts playtime and reports it from login. Without it `addUsageTime` had
  no caller at all, so a web title reported **zero** active users no matter how many people played:
  DAU, WAU, MAU, stickiness and every retention cohort are derived from what it sends. Flush
  interval and idle threshold match the Unity SDK so the two platforms count the same thing.
- **`IDosGamesSettings.appVersion`** — the build number that rides along with the acquisition
  signal. The web has no `Application.version`, so the host has to pass it; without it no player is
  attributed to a release and cohort-by-version is unanswerable.
- **`UserReferralState.Code`** — the player's own short invite code, minted lazily by the server on
  the first `getUserState()`.
- **`UserReferralState.PendingActivationReward`** — set when the binding happened at login rather
  than by typing a code; the debt is settled by the next `getUserState()`.
- **`UserReferralStateResponse.InviteUrl`** — a ready-made invite link built by the server. Do not
  assemble one from a template: a client-built link is an open redirect.
- **`SpendRewardDefinition`** gains `Basis`, `MinSourceAmount`, `MaxRewardPerOperation` and
  `Limits` — the anti-farm controls that existed on the server and could not be expressed here.
- **`PlatformAdapter.getReferrer?()`** — optional, so existing custom adapters keep compiling.

### Fixed

- **Playtime was lost on every tab switch.** `visibilitychange` fires _after_ the state flips, so
  the tracker asked the document, was told "hidden", and discarded the visible stretch that led up
  to the switch — up to a full flush interval, every time.
- **Response schemas no longer strip unknown fields.** `zUserReferralStateResponse`,
  `zActivateReferralCodeResponse`, `zClaimInviteRewardResponse` and
  `zReferralDefinitionsResponse` were missing `.passthrough()`, so `InviteUrl` never reached the
  client at all.

## [0.9.0] - 2026-08-24

Signing in by e-mail becomes a **two-step flow** with a confirmation code, and a password now
belongs to a **title**, not to the platform. Friend requests gain the outgoing direction, and the
usage history is rolled up into periods. Breaking — see below.

### Breaking

- **`registerWithEmail` no longer signs the player in.** It returns `EmailRegistrationOutcome`
  (`codeTtlMinutes`, `resendCooldownSeconds`) instead of `ClientState`: the server only stores the
  attempt and mails a code, and the player is created by `confirmEmailRegistration`. A screen that
  waits for a session here waits forever. There is no flag to branch on — confirmation is platform
  behaviour and no title can switch it off.
- **`EMAIL_ALREADY_EXISTS` is no longer returned by registration.** A free and a taken address
  answer identically, so the form cannot be used to ask "does this person have an account here";
  the owner of a taken address gets a "you already have an account" e-mail instead, without a code.
- **`loginWithPlatformToken` and `AuthenticationAction.LoginWithPlatformToken` removed.** The
  backend stopped issuing the audience it accepted, so the endpoint was unreachable code. Use
  `loginWithSsoCode` (see `beginSsoRedirect`).
- **`UserReferralState.FollowerIDs` removed.** It was an unbounded list in the hot player document
  with no readers; the count that replaced it is server-sent, and the relationship itself lives on
  the subscriber's side.

### Added

- **`confirmEmailRegistration(email, code)`** — exchanges the mailed code for a session and creates
  the player. Persists the credentials for `autoLogin()` exactly as `loginWithEmail` does; the
  password comes from step one and is never sent again.
- **`resendVerificationCode(email)`** — mails a NEW code (only a hash is stored server-side, so the
  previous one cannot be re-sent). Answers successfully whatever happened, with one exception worth
  surfacing: `EMAIL_SENDER_NOT_CONFIGURED`, which is about the server's configuration and not about
  the address.
- **`zEmailRegistrationResponse` / `EmailRegistrationResponse`** and
  `AuthenticationRequest.VerificationCode`.
- **`client.social.getOutgoingRequests()`** + `SocialAction.GetOutgoingRequests` and the
  `social:outgoingRequestsLoaded` event. Direction and status are separate axes, and the outgoing
  list cannot be derived from a counter — without it the "Sent" mark on a card lived only until the
  app restarted.
- **`UserSocialState.FriendsCount` / `IncomingCount` / `OutgoingCount`** — server-sent counters.
  The friend lists themselves are now a local cache, filled by the matching `get*` call.
- **`UsagePeriodRecord`** — the rolled-up month/year record (`Seconds`, `Sessions`, `ActiveDays`,
  `LongestSessionSeconds`, `ActiveHoursMask`, `FirstActiveDay`).
- **`BoardRollResponse.DiceValues`** — the individual dice behind the rolled total.

### Changed

- ⚠ **A password now belongs to the TITLE.** The same address in two games means two independent
  passwords, and resetting in one game does not change the login for the other. The reset e-mail
  goes out through the **publisher's** SMTP, so a shared password would let one publisher's mail
  server control access to every other publisher's game. The identity stays shared — Google, Apple
  and the idosgames.com sign-in still recognise the same person everywhere; identity answers "who
  is this", not "what proves they may sign in". Don't tell the player "the same password as in your
  other game", and don't reuse stored credentials across titles.
- **Every outcome of `resetPassword` answers the same** — `INVALID_RESET_CODE` for an unknown
  address, a code never requested, an expired code and a wrong code alike; an exhausted code
  answers `RESET_CODE_ATTEMPTS_EXCEEDED`. The remaining-attempt count is gone from the response: it
  confirmed the account existed and told an attacker how much room was left. Don't parse a number
  out of `error`.

## [0.7.0] - 2026-08-10

Real-money payment support. Every configured price becomes a **`PriceOptions` dictionary**, a
store SKU becomes one of the ways to pay, and the client now tells the server which platform it
runs on. Breaking — see below.

### Added

- **`PriceOption` / `PriceOptions` (`zPriceOption`, `zPriceOptions`)** — the platform-wide price
  standard. A `ResourceConsume` is charged as a whole ("and"); a price across platforms is a
  choice ("or") — a store SKU on mobile, a token on web. The dictionary key is the `OptionID`,
  and the server substitutes it when the field is empty.
- **`ResourceEntryType.Purchase` + `ResourceEntry.ProductID`** — an entry that means "paid in a
  store". `ProductID` addresses `Purchase.Products`, our stable id, not a per-store SKU.
- **`PaymentProof` (`zPaymentProof`)** — the receipt attached to a request. Required exactly when
  the chosen option holds a `Purchase` entry: the server never takes money itself, it verifies
  what the store issued to this client.
- **`client.purchase` (`PurchaseService`)** — `getDefinitions`, `getUserState`,
  `validatePurchase`, `validatePurchasesBatch`. `Resources` is applied only when `Granted` is
  true: `AlreadyProcessed` and `Restored` carry the same block, and crediting it would pay the
  reward twice for one payment — which is exactly what a store's re-delivered receipt looks like.
- **`client.checkout` (`CheckoutService`)** — `availableOptions`, `isAvailable`, `requirementOf`,
  `storeProductOf`, `cryptoShortfallOf`. It deliberately buys nothing: the purchase belongs to the
  module that owns the entity (`client.store.purchase`, `client.lootbox.open`, …), which is the
  only place that knows count, target ids and the idempotency key.
- **`ClientPlatform`** (`Unknown | Web | Android | Ios`) and `IDosGamesClientConfig.clientPlatform`.
  Auto-detected by `detectClientPlatform()` and sent as **`X-IG-Platform`** on every request —
  once, in the transport, because a service that forgot to pass it would silently get a different
  price list. Detection is conservative: a browser is `Web` even on a phone, only a real native
  wrapper (Capacitor / Cordova) counts as `Android`/`Ios`, and no `navigator` at all is `Unknown`
  rather than `Web`.
- `SegmentGate.Platforms` — gate any definition on the client platform.
- Optional **`selectedOptionID`** on every call that charges a configured price —
  `store.purchase`, `lootbox.open`, `craft.craft`, `premium.purchaseItemOrCurrency`,
  `character.unlockCharacter`, `collection.openPack`, `dealOffer.executeNode`,
  `timedBoost.activate`, `item.upgradeLevel`, `coopEvent.spin`, `gameLoop.boardSpecialChoose`,
  `match.createMatch`, `marketplace.createListing` / `createAuction`. Omitting it keeps
  single-price entities working with no client change: the server takes the first option
  available on this platform.
- Optional **`payment`** (a `PaymentProof`) on the calls the server can settle against a store
  receipt: `store.purchase`, `lootbox.open`, `character.unlockCharacter`, `collection.openPack`,
  `dealOffer.executeNode`, `timedBoost.activate`. The rest deliberately have none — an upgrade
  priced by a level formula, a per-fact coop spin, a refundable listing fee and a P2P match stake
  cannot be one store SKU, and the server rejects a `Purchase` entry in those places.

### Changed

- **Every price field is now `PriceOptions`.** `StoreOfferDefinition.Cost`,
  `CraftDefinition.RequiredResources`, `LootboxDefinition.PriceOptions` (was a list of
  `LootboxPriceOption`), `PremiumDefinition.PriceOptions`, `CollectionPackDefinition.Cost`,
  `CharacterDefinition.Unlock.Cost` / stat & level `BaseCostResource` / `UpgradeCost`,
  `ItemUpgrade.BaseCostResource`, `TimedBoostDefinition.ActivationCost`,
  `CoopEventBuildObjects.SpinCost`, `GameLoop` special-mode choice `EntryCost`,
  `DealOfferPurchaseAction.DirectCost`, `MatchCreationSettings.Cost`,
  `MarketplaceListingSettings.ListingFee` — all replaced by a `PriceOptions` dictionary.
- `lootbox.open`'s `selectedOptionID` is a **string** (was `number`) and is now optional.
- Prices come back **already filtered by the request's platform**, and the charge re-checks it.
  The client renders what the server gave; a hidden option cannot be paid anyway.

### Removed

- **`ResourceEntryType.UsdCent`** — it was declared but never worked (any operation with it
  failed inside the inventory layer), so a price in real money looked configurable while the
  entity was impossible to buy. `Purchase` replaces it.

### Migration

Read a price through `client.checkout.availableOptions(entity.PriceOptions)` instead of the old
single cost field, and pass the chosen `OptionID` to the module's buying call. A price paid in a
store additionally needs a `PaymentProof` — buy in the store first, then hand the receipt to the
same call. Nothing else changes for entities that keep a single price.

## [0.6.0] - 2026-08-09

### Added

- **`client.tutorial` (`TutorialService`)** — onboarding flows: `getTutorialDefinitions`,
  `getUserTutorialState`, `startFlow`, `reportStepShown`, `completeStep`,
  `completeStepsBatch`, `skipStep`, `skipFlow`, `claimFlowReward`, `resetFlow`. Definitions
  are cached like the rest of the title config.
- **Tutorial progress rides on every response.** A tutorial step is usually closed by an
  ordinary game action (a purchase, a dice roll), not by a tutorial call — so the backend puts
  an optional `TutorialProgress` block into the envelope of **any** response, the transport
  lifts it out, and `UserData` merges it into the state. Subscribe to `tutorial:systemProgress`
  instead of polling `getUserTutorialState`: the state is already fresh after any request, and
  polling also skews the `ReportStepShown` funnel.
- `SegmentGate.Tutorial` (`TutorialGateCondition` / `TutorialGateMode`) — gate any module's
  definitions on the player's onboarding progress.
- **`client.localization` (`LocalizationService`)** — `t(key, params)`, `has`, `locale`,
  `fallbackLocale`, `locales`, `setLocale`, `getManifest`. Resolution is
  **own table → fallback table → the key itself**, so a title whose config holds literal
  display names ("Iron Sword") keeps working without migration: the literal is a key with no
  translation. Plural forms come from `Intl.PluralRules` (suffixes `.one/.few/.many/.other`).
- Translation tables arrive **with the player state** — no separate load. `UserService` sends
  the locale and the versions of the tables it already has and resolves what comes back
  through the same source chain as the title config (storage → CDN → endpoint → stale copy),
  with one deliberate difference: a failure here does **not** fail the login. No config means
  nothing to play; no translations means the UI shows keys.
- `settings.locale` (`SettingsInput.locale`) — the starting locale, defaulting to the device
  language. It is a **wish**, not a fact: the server folds it to what the title is actually
  translated into (`pt-BR` → `pt` → `en`), and the answer is `client.localization.locale`.
- `TitlePublicConfigurationModel.Localization` — locale settings only. The tables are
  delivered separately, one file per locale.
- `localization:changed` event (login, `setLocale`, new tables). `t()` is synchronous, so
  already-rendered labels need this signal to repaint.
- `PostOptions.throttleKey` — override the throttle / in-flight-dedup key when one route
  serves genuinely different requests back to back. Added for the localization tables: own and
  fallback both go through `Localization/GetLocalizationTable`, and under the default key
  (the endpoint) the second call would be dropped as a duplicate — the fallback table would
  never arrive, silently, and only for players whose language is partially translated. The
  throttle window still applies, just per key.
- **Batch claims** — `season.claimTierRewardsBatch(seasonChainID, tierNumbers)` and
  `referral.claimInviteRewardsBatch(inviteRewardIDs)`. Season tiers in particular are reached
  in batches: one token grant can raise a player through several at once. The merged
  `Resources` is applied **once** from the top level; per-item `Data.Resources` is null by
  contract so summing both cannot double count.
- **Multi-open ceilings** — `collection.openPack(collectionID, packTypeID, count?)`,
  `collection.openCollectionChest(collectionID, chestID, count?)` and
  `coopEvent.spin(chainID, groupID, count?)` open/spin `count` times in one atomic operation
  (`count` defaults to 1, so existing calls are unaffected). Each roll sees the state left by
  the previous one, so a repeat drop is correctly counted as a duplicate. The count is clamped
  server-side; responses report what actually happened (`OpenedCount` + per-item `Packs` /
  `Chests`, `RequestedSpins` / `SpinsUsed` / `Sectors`). Only spins that happen are charged —
  a run stops at the spin that completes the object.
- Config for those ceilings: `LootboxDefinitions.Settings` (`LootboxGlobalSettings`) and
  `LootboxDefinition.MaxOpenCount`, `CollectionDefinitions.Settings`
  (`CollectionGlobalSettings`), `CollectionPackTypeDefinition.MaxOpenCount`,
  `CollectionChestDefinition.MaxOpenCount`, `CoopBuildObjectsDefinition.MaxSpinsPerCall`.
- `FriendActionResponse.Target` (the other side's public profile) and `.Counters`
  (`SocialCounters`) — a new friend can be shown without a second `getFriendsList()`.
- New events: `tutorial:definitionsLoaded` / `:userStateLoaded` / `:flowStarted` /
  `:flowSkipped` / `:flowReset` / `:stepChanged` / `:stepsCompletedBatch` / `:rewardClaimed` /
  `:systemProgress`, `localization:changed`, `season:tierRewardsBatchClaimed`,
  `referral:inviteRewardsBatchClaimed`, `user:tutorialUpdated`.

### Notes

- Everything here is additive: the new `count` parameters default to `1`, the new response
  fields are optional, and no existing signature changed.
- `TutorialStepPolicy.TimeoutSeconds` is carried in the schema but **not applied** — neither
  the backend (it has no "N seconds passed" moment) nor `core` (it renders no UI) can enforce
  it. Whoever draws the tutorial implements it, and only for `ClientAck` steps; on a step
  waiting for a game event the backend rejects `completeStep`.

## [0.5.1] - 2026-08-05

Version-only republish of 0.5.0 — no source changes.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-08-04

### Added

- `auth.loginWithSsoCode(code)` — exchange a one-time code issued by idosgames.com for a
  title session. This is how a game signs a player in without ever receiving a platform
  token: the code lives 60 seconds, is burnt on first exchange, and only works for the
  title it was issued for. Deliberately **not** replayable by `autoLogin()` — a stale
  session is re-established by bouncing through `/sso` again, which is silent while the
  site session is alive.
- `readSsoCodeFromUrl()` — read that code out of the URL fragment and strip it from the
  address bar (a fragment never reaches a server, so it stays out of proxy logs and
  `Referer`; clearing it stops a reload from re-submitting a burnt code). Verifies the
  returned `state` against the one this browser stored before leaving.
- `beginSsoRedirect({titleID, returnTo?, ssoUrl?})` — send the browser to the platform
  sign-in page. Top-level redirect rather than a popup: popups are blocked by default on
  mobile browsers and inside standalone/PWA windows, which is exactly where games run.
- `AuthenticationAction.LoginWithSsoCode` and `AuthenticationRequest.SsoCode`.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-06-29

### Added

- Engine-agnostic core client (`createIDosGamesClient` / `IDosGamesClient`) that owns the
  whole SDK graph: HTTP transport (retry, in-flight dedup, throttle, transparent 401
  re-login), auth, local cache, and a typed event bus.
- 24 feature domains exposed as services on the client: `auth`, `user`, `currency`,
  `item`, `store`, `lootbox`, `reward`, `quest`, `timedEvent`, `leaderboard`, `season`,
  `premium`, `character`, `match`, `craft`, `collection`, `coopEvent`, `dealOffer`,
  `referral`, `social`, `timedBoost`, `userCustomData`, `title`, `gameLoop`.
- `OperationResult<T>` discriminated result type — services never throw on expected
  failures; callers branch on `result.ok`.
- zod-validated response models (the schema is the source of truth via `z.infer`).
- Platform adapters (`BrowserPlatformAdapter`, `NoopPlatformAdapter`) plus the
  `@idosgames/core/platform` subpath export.

---

The game templates `@idosgames/board-game` and `@idosgames/idle-rpg` live in this repo
as **starter projects** and are intentionally **not** published to npm; they are not
tracked in this changelog.
